subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key, default, and ASCII replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but naming and behavior for a new public config surface become compatibility contracts and should be chosen by maintainers before implementation.

options.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
options.body: Implement an opt-in core setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, generated config metadata, public docs, and tests while retaining current glyph output by default.

options.title: Defer until config shape is chosen
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide the public key, default, and replacement semantics before implementation starts.

options.title: Reject core config for now
options.body: Close only if maintainers explicitly decide glyph suppression should not be a core TUI capability despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Implement an opt-in core setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, generated config metadata, public docs, and tests while retaining current glyph output by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is original TUI/tool-display ownership plus current config/TUI ownership evidence.
